message.content: In lions, one of the most well‑documented dominant traits is the **presence of a mane** in adult males. The gene(s) that control mane development act in a dominant fashion: if a male inherits the allele that promotes mane growth, he will develop a mane regardless of the allele inherited from the other parent. This trait is highly heritable and is strongly associated with male body size, testosterone levels, and social status within prides.
